newsitem.title: GERMANY: German "wise man"-Buba, EMU credibility at risk.
newsitem.headline: German "wise man"-Buba, EMU credibility at risk.

text.p: A key adviser to the German government said on Thursday that the open battle between Bonn and the Bundesbank held serious risks for the credibility of the German central bank and Europe's monetary union.

Rolf Peffekoven, a member of the Council of Economic Advisers dubbed Germany's "Five Wise Men", said on radio that the row over whether Bonn should be allowed to upwardly value Bundesbank gold and currency reserves was "exceptionally threatening to the autonomy and credibility of the Bundesbank".
Yet more dangerous was the issue to the project of monetary union itself, he added, noting that the Bundesbank had always been held up as an example of strength to other central banks.
"It is now going to be hard to get over the idea that a future European Central bank will be immune from political attacks," he warned.

Bonn's plan to derive extra revenues from a revaluation of Bundesbank gold and currency reserves was in any case faulty in that it would be difficult for any impact to show up in the budget for 1997, the crucial year for EMU qualification, he added.
